interest: Shows State's shift from non-intervention to urgently stalling a Japanese insurer's $1 million transfer just before the 1941 freeze.
overview: This decimal file (894.506 Insurance) documents communications between New York State Superintendent of Insurance Louis H. Pink and officials of the U.S. Department of State—principally Adviser on International Economic Affairs Herbert Feis, Assistant Secretary Dean Acheson, and the Division of Far Eastern Affairs—between December 1940 and July 1941 concerning the liquidation and repatriation of Japanese and Italian insurance assets. Throughout late 1940 and May 1941, New York insurance authorities permitted the release of millions of dollars in surplus and free funds to Japanese companies (notably the Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Company, Ltd.) and oversaw stock transactions with American firms such as Aetna Insurance Company, with the State Department repeatedly declining to intervene. However, as tensions mounted and American assets in Japan were increasingly restricted, internal debates within the State Department weighed capital controls and bilateral negotiations against concerns about discriminatory treatment. By early July 1941, on the eve of the United States freezing all Japanese assets, State Department policy pivoted sharply, culminating in an urgent request to Superintendent Pink to find any way to stall and defer a pending $1,000,000 remittance by Tokio Marine for several weeks.
